import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify strong candidates by t-statistic and effect size
    t_stats = []
    effect_sizes = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical':
            continue  # Skip clinical features for now
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
        effect_size = np.mean(y1) - np.mean(y0)
        t_stats.append(abs(t_stat))
        effect_sizes.append(abs(effect_size))
    
    # Select top features based on t-statistics
    top_indices = np.argsort(t_stats)[::-1][:20]
    candidates = [feats.ids[i] for i in top_indices]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates
    unique_candidates = []
    seen = set()
    for fid in candidates:
        if any(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)], 
                           feats.x[:, feats.column(other_fid)])[0,1] > 0.6 
               for other_fid in seen if other_fid != fid):
            continue
        unique_candidates.append(fid)
        seen.add(fid)
    
    # Use only top 4 unique candidates (as per checker report)
    selected = unique_candidates[:4]
    
    # Build regression components
    drivers = tuple(selected)
    columns = tuple(selected)
    
    # Add interaction terms for top 3
    products = []
    for i in range(min(3, len(selected))):
        for j in range(i+1, min(3, len(selected))):
            products.append((selected[i], selected[j]))
    
    # Simple weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, fid in enumerate(selected):
        loadings[fid] = float(effect_sizes[i])
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
